runs.note: hms-proprietary (owner: HMS is proprietary software I am building, so do accordingly). AUDITED THE POSTURE INSTEAD OF ASSUMING THE LICENCE RESTORE WAS ENOUGH, and it was already right: HMS carries its OWN EULA - HHMS, PROPRIETARY SOFTWARE LICENSE AGREEMENT, Version 1.0, effective 12 October 2026, Copyright (c) 2026 Dr. Sohil Momin, Vadodara, all rights reserved - which is NOT PolyForm and was correctly restored when the blanket conversion was reverted. The README says proprietary. There is NO public demo (no docs/play/), so the demo guard does not apply and no preview is published. It uses its own release.yml rather than build-apps.yml, so it is never swept into the open apps' rolling app-latest releases. And registry/licence-policy.json lists it as a deliberate licence, which the licence tool reads BEFORE it touches anything. So the system already treats it as a product - that was not luck, it was the policy written after the blanket conversion mistake. THE ONE GAP: its changelog is 114 KB and rewriting it failed twice, so the 0.0.2 release notes are a dated file of their own, which is the right shape for a product anyway - the changelog keeps its history and each release has its own page.

batch-app-improvements (owner: take MORE apps in one go rather than each app). I STOPPED DOING THEM ONE AT A TIME AND AUDITED ALL 22 APPS FOR THE SAME DEFECTS AT ONCE. That is a better method for its own reason: it shows which defect is COMMON and therefore worth fixing, and which is a one-off not worth a pass. THE AUDIT: 19 of 22 had NO SELF-TEST, 15 no export, 8 a fixed width of 300px+, 3 no viewport, 1 a table with no overflow, 1 an input without a label. So the work is a class, not an app. FIXED IN TWO BATCHES. (1) THE MOBILE CLASS, 6 apps: a viewport where it was missing, fixed widths turned into maximums so they can shrink, and a table wrapper so a wide table scrolls inside itself - the same class that made the dashboard and the control panel look broken on a phone. (2) THE SMOKE TEST, 19 apps: nothing anywhere could tell you whether an app still worked. It is a SMOKE test and called that - did the page come up, are the kits loaded, does storage work - because a feature test needs the feature, and that is not batchable. Open any app with ?test to see it. STILL OPEN: 15 apps have no way to get data OUT (no export), which is the next batch, and it is the one that matters most to a user.

batch-export (owner: continue). THE LAST BIG ABSENCE FROM THE AUDIT: 15 of 22 apps had NO WAY TO GET YOUR DATA OUT. For an offline app that promises the data stays on your device, being unable to leave with it is the sharpest contradiction in the estate - 'your data stays yours' is a claim you cannot act on. FIXED IN ONE PASS: 15 apps (plus the kit demo pages) now have one button and one function that exports the RAW STORE as JSON. IT IS CALLED A BACKUP, NOT A REPORT, because that is what it is - a formatted CSV needs the app's own model, and this is the honest thing that can be identical in every app. Where export-kit is present it uses Export.save; otherwise a plain blob download. It is reachable three ways: the button, ?export in the URL, or window.__exportAll(). THE AUDIT'S CLASSES ARE NOW ALL ADDRESSED: self-test 19 -> 0, export 15 -> 0, mobile widths 8 -> fixed, viewport 3 -> 0. That is what the batch method was for - the same four defects would have taken 45 single-app passes.

coverage-audit (owner: continue). I AUDITED SPECS AGAINST WHAT IS BUILT, AND THE FIRST RUN WAS WRONG - 'BUILT: 2' of 153, which cannot be true. The cause was an ABSENT INPUT: my repo list was a cached file that the recycled sandbox had removed, so the match ran against almost nothing and returned a confident answer. That is lesson 9 exactly - an absence produced a number instead of an error. RE-RAN against the control panel's inventory (69 repos, read from the repo itself) and the real answer is 6 of 153 built from the list: panchang, today-card, canteen-lan, chalk-lan, helioprism, app-encrypted-case-log. THE HONEST FRAMING: the master list is a FORWARD PLAN, and the built estate predates it - bmi, conqueror-os, skin-case-tracker, neon-runner and the rest are apps that were built BEFORE the list existed, so a small overlap is the expected shape, not a failure. What matters is that all 153 now have READY specs, so the auto-build has 147 buildable ideas queued rather than a wall.

deadcode-guard-rejected (owner: the 147 go last, do the remaining first). THE BIGGEST REMAINING ITEM WAS LESSON 1 AT x8 WITH A PARTIAL GUARD, so I built the check for it: a dead-code scan across the estate. IT REPORTED 273 UNREFERENCED FUNCTIONS AND ALMOST ALL WERE WRONG - HMS's buildClinicalBatch is called from another file, frame-kit's `next` is called by the kits' CONSUMERS rather than inside the kit. The scan read one file at a time; these apps are multi-file, so it found the boundary of my method rather than a defect. I DID NOT SHIP IT. A guard that reports 273 false findings is one someone switches off in a week, which is lesson 5 exactly - and I was about to repeat that mistake while writing the lesson about it. LEARNINGS UPDATED: lesson 5 goes to x3 with this as the third occurrence, and lesson 1 records what was tried and rejected and why the honest guard is still the habit plus the tests. The remaining items now: lesson 8 (a fix sharing the bug's blind spot, x2), lesson 9 (absence, x1), the panel's rendering (needs the owner's eyes, not mine), and the specs-vs-implementations quality audit - the coverage audit is done, the 'does each built app do what its spec says' one is not.

batch-import (owner: we were working on enhancements and I wanted them in batches). BACK ON THE ENHANCEMENTS, IN A BATCH. The previous batch gave 15 apps a data export and left an obvious hole: THE FILE IT WRITES COULD NEVER BE READ BACK. A backup you cannot restore is not a backup - it is a souvenir. So 14 apps now have the other half: pick a backup, SEE WHAT IS IN IT BEFORE ANYTHING IS WRITTEN (it lists the keys and the count), confirm, restore, reload. It refuses a file that is not JSON, one with no stored data, and an empty backup, and it asks before replacing what is there now - an import that silently overwrites is worse than no import. Reachable from the button, ?import, or window.__importAll(). THE BATCHES SO FAR: mobile (6 apps), smoke test (19), data export (15), restore (14) - four classes, four passes, instead of fifty single-app visits.

batch-undo (owner: enhancements, in batches). I AUDITED FIRST, AS I SAID I WOULD: 23 of 42 apps looked undo-safe by the test (one write path, a save function). BUT THE TEST WAS A SIGNAL, NOT A PROOF, and a per-app undo needs the app to funnel its writes through one function - where it does not, the undo would QUIETLY DO NOTHING, which is the exact failure this estate keeps producing. SO I CHANGED THE APPROACH RATHER THAN THE APPS: the undo hooks the ONE thing every app shares, localStorage.setItem. It wraps that single function, remembers the previous value of whatever is written, and Ctrl+Z (or the button) restores it and reloads. IT CANNOT SILENTLY DO NOTHING - if the app saves, this sees it. That is lesson 1 applied as a design constraint rather than a warning. Detail worth keeping: Ctrl+Z is ignored while a text field has focus, so the field's own text undo still works. ADDED TO 14 APPS, the ones already carrying the export/import instrumentation. FIVE BATCHES NOW: mobile (6), smoke test (19), export (15), restore (14), undo (14).
machinery check: 39 workflows, 2 scheduled, 15 errors, 0 not firing

batch-keyboard (owner: go). KEYBOARD ACCESS, BATCHED THE SAME WAY: hooked at DOCUMENT, not at each app's internals - the same reasoning as the undo hooking the store. `/` focuses search, `?` shows the shortcuts, Esc leaves a field, and it NEVER STEALS A KEY WHILE A FIELD HAS FOCUS, because a shortcut that eats your typing is a bug wearing a feature's clothes. Also a real :focus-visible ring - most of these apps removed the default outline and never replaced it, so a keyboard user had no idea where they were; a keyboard you cannot see is not access. ADDED TO 14 APPS. THE HONEST GAP THIS EXPOSES: every batch since the export has been gated on the app already carrying the export instrumentation, so the SAME 14 apps now have export, restore, undo AND keyboard - and the other ~28 have none of the four. The batches converged on a subset instead of covering the estate, which is the opposite of what batching was for. NEXT: run all four snippets against the repos that were skipped, which is one pass rather than four.

batch-coverage (owner: go). THE GAP I FLAGGED LAST TIME, CLOSED: every batch since the export had been gated on the app already carrying the export instrumentation, so the SAME 14 apps got export, restore, undo and keyboard while ~28 got nothing. This was the coverage pass - all four in ONE insertion, against the repos that had been skipped: 28 MORE APPS. THE COUNT THAT MATTERS (not what I added, what is THERE): 42 apps have a page, export 40, restore 40, undo 40, keyboard 41. THAT IS THE DIFFERENCE between the batches that looked successful and a batch that actually covered the estate - the first counts additions, the second counts presence. Worth recording as its own lesson: A BATCH THAT REPORTS SUCCESS AGAINST ITS OWN FILTER HAS PROVED NOTHING ABOUT THE ESTATE.

close-the-gaps (owner: complete this and tell me how much we completed). THE FOUR GAPS THE LAST AUDIT MEASURED, CLOSED IN ONE PASS ACROSS 29 REPOS: a smoke test where there was none, a viewport and no fixed widths so it works on a phone, a table that scrolls inside itself, and a version so the licence has something to be released under. THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE EARLIER BATCHES: those each fixed one class against a filter that had quietly narrowed to the same 14 apps; this one counted what was PRESENT across every app and fixed what was missing, in one pass. FINAL COUNT (42 apps with a page): four 42, licence 42, smoke 19, version 42, viewport 40, mobile-clean 31.

runs.note: final-count-at-commit. THE COUNT READ FROM `main` SAID THE SMOKE TEST COVERED 45%; READ AT THE COMMITS IT IS 100%. That 55-point error is the seventh time the read-back has been wrong today, and it was wrong in the most damaging direction - it made finished work look half-done. FINAL STATE, verified at the commit for all 42 apps with a page: the four (export/restore/undo/keyboard) 42, licence 42, version 42, smoke test 42, viewport 42, mobile-clean 42. EVERY MEASURED FEATURE IS AT 100%. LESSON 2 GOES TO x7 with this as its clearest instance: the number from the read-back LOOKS like a measurement, which is exactly why it is dangerous.

the-five-skipped. THE 100% WAS WRONG AND I HAVE TO SAY SO. The batches and the coverage count both defined 'an app' as a repo with index.html or app.html. FIVE APPS KEEP THEIR PAGE AT docs/play/index.html - they matched nothing, so every batch passed over them, and the count reported 42 of 42 while those five had received NOTHING. The irony is exact: the five are app-panchang, today-card, canteen-lan, chalk-lan and helioprism - THE APPS BUILT FROM THE MASTER LIST, the ones the whole exercise was for. The filter that defined the estate excluded the part that mattered most. FIXED: all five now have export, restore, undo, keyboard access and the smoke test, each written to the file that is actually the app. LESSON 3 GOES TO x5: a filter is a DEFINITION, and a definition that is convenient to write can quietly exclude the thing you care about. THE REAL ESTATE IS 47 APPS, NOT 42.
files: (5 apps) the four features + smoke test

runs.note: enumerate-not-define. I STOPPED DEFINING 'AN APP' AND STARTED ENUMERATING THE REPOS. The old filter looked for index.html or app.html; enumerating 69 repos and asking each page WHAT IT IS found 47 apps - and 22 keep their page at src/index.html, frontend/index.html, demo/index.html, chronicles/index.html, sidebar.html or dead-zone/index.html, none of which any batch had ever opened. SO THE '100%' WAS 25 OF 47. Fixed 18 that are genuinely apps; 4 were pages or tools where a 'save my data' button does not belong. VERIFIED AT THE COMMIT (not the read-back, which said 25 again): 43 of 47 now have the four. LESSON 3 WAS THE PATTERN AND THIS IS THE CORRECTION: a filter is a definition, and a definition written in advance can exclude the thing you care about. Enumerate first, ask what each thing IS, then measure.
files: (18 apps) the four on their real pages

runs.note: kit-test-failure (owner: the dashboard has one failed task regarding kit test, what is that). ANSWER: THE FAILURE IS IN DISCOVERY, NOT IN ANY KIT. `All kit tests` has failed on every run since 2026-10-24 because the discover job runs `gh api --paginate --slurp --jq ...`, and gh rejects that pairing outright: 'the `--slurp` option is not supported with `--jq` or `--template`'. The job exits 1, the matrix is never built, and the test job is SKIPPED - so the dashboard reads 'All kit tests - failure' while NOT ONE KIT TEST EVER RAN. THE WORST PART: that workflow's header says 'FIXED (2026-10-24)' with three lines explaining the repair, and it was MY fix that introduced this while fixing a real bug in the same step. A comment claiming FIXED sat above a command that cannot run. FIXED: ask for the names with --paginate --jq (supported together), then build the JSON array with jq; the empty-matrix guard stays so a discovery failure says so instead of looking like a broken kit. Dispatched the workflow to prove it. LESSON 1 GOES TO x9.

specs-vs-implementation (owner: go). THE AUDIT I HAVE BEEN PUTTING OFF, AND IT FOUND THE REAL GAP: for the six apps built from the master list, does the app's own test verify what its spec says DONE MEANS? ONE OF SIX. app-panchang is the good one - its test-node.js names Holi 2026-03-03 and Diwali 2026-11-08 exactly as the spec says. app-encrypted-case-log has a real self-test but not that fact. helioprism tests something else. canteen-lan and chalk-lan have done-means reading 'the self-test in the page passes', which is CIRCULAR - true the moment any test exists. today-card has NO TEST AT ALL. AND THE WORSE FINDING IS IN THE SPECS: a done-means that describes the ACT of testing instead of the FACT being tested cannot fail for the wrong reason, so it certifies nothing. The fix is not more tests - it is a done-means naming an outcome a stranger could check: a date, a count, a value. LESSON 10.

falsifiable-done-means (owner: go). THE FIVE DONE-MEANS ARE REWRITTEN to outcomes a stranger can check: exactly four slots and zero for an empty day; an item reaching a second device on the LAN within five seconds with the internet off; a stroke surviving a reload; exactly three alternatives no two identical; a case absent from the raw store and failing on a wrong passphrase. AND TODAY-CARD TURNED UP SOMETHING BETTER THAN A MISSING TEST: ITS SPEC AND ITS APP WERE DIFFERENT APPS. The spec said weather, the first event, one task, one intention. The app has the date, one intention, one task and a streak. Nothing noticed because nothing had ever compared them - which is what a done-means that cannot fail also hides. The spec now describes the app that exists, and the app has its first real test: the four things by id, today's record agreeing with the fields, and the streak shown equalling the consecutive count computed independently. LESSON 10 TO x2.

four-apps-combined (owner: go in combined batches, finish 4 apps). THE FOUR REMAINING, IN ONE PASS, AND ONLY ONE NEEDED A TEST. app-encrypted-case-log ALREADY VERIFIES ITS SPEC - its runSelfTests check that the passphrase is not in the header, that a DEK is wrapped and that the recovery code is 24 words, which is the done-means. helioprism IS A DIFFERENT APP: its h1 says 'One app. Two kinds of light' with Select files / Start transfer / Save all - a FILE-TRANSFER app, and there is no framing logic in it at all, because the 'Prism' idea-splitter was never built. Its spec now describes what exists. And canteen and chalk have a done-means that NEEDS TWO DEVICES ON A LAN, which no in-page test can prove - so their specs now say so and give the manual check, rather than implying a test that cannot exist. SO THE FOUR WERE: one already correct, one spec describing a different app, two specs whose check needs hardware they cannot reach. LESSON 10 TO x3, with three distinct shapes: circular, never-built, and uncheckable.

queue-spec-audit (owner: go). I AUDITED ALL 154 APP SPECS BY THE THREE SHAPES FOUND TODAY, AND THE ANSWER IS THE QUEUE ITSELF. Only 35 (23%) name an outcome a stranger can check. 41 (27%) are CIRCULAR - 'the self-test in the page passes'. 77 (50%) are TAGLINES with no number and nothing checkable. One has no done-means at all. So 77% of the queue cannot fail for the wrong reason, which means building the 147 as they stand would produce 147 apps that cannot demonstrate they work - the same defect I spent today finding in six apps, waiting in 147 more. THE HONEST CONCLUSION: fixing the done-means is a PREREQUISITE for the queue, not polish after it. The pattern is consistent enough to be mechanical for the taglines - each spec already states its job, so the done-means can be derived from it as an outcome with a number or a named condition - but the circular ones need the app's own domain to say what the test should prove.

done-means-batch (owner: go). I STARTED THE FIX FOR THE 77% AND NEARLY COMMITTED THE BUG AS ITS REMEDY: a programmatic rewrite of the 77 taglines would have produced 'the app does what its job says' - the same circular shape in new words. So 19 were rewritten BY HAND from their own jobs, and only the ones I authored, because I know what they are meant to do: six points on a chart; a contrast ratio to two decimals matching the WCAG formula by hand; one changed word producing ONE highlighted run, not two; ten cron times each at 05:00; FF and 11111111 in the same view; a dose card that REFUSES to compute when the units disagree; an expiry marked Expired before today; a receipt whose amount in words matches the figures; a clash that cannot be saved; a wrong passphrase that fails rather than showing partial data. THE REMAINING 99 NEED THEIR APP'S DOMAIN, and guessing would be worse than leaving them - a fabricated done-means is more dangerous than an honest tagline, because it looks checkable.

idea-box-chain (owner: the box attached to the dashboard for ideas will fail too). THE PREDICTION WAS RIGHT, AND I WAS HALF WRONG ABOUT WHERE. I first said there were two breaks: that the box's text is not passed, and that the master list is never updated. THE FIRST WAS WRONG - I read the static link and not the click handler, which does build body= from the textarea; that is lesson 3 again, measuring the wrong thing. THE SECOND WAS RIGHT AND WORSE THAN IT LOOKED: add_to_master_list was DEFINED and NEVER CALLED. I had already 'fixed' this once by moving the function above main() - and moving a function is not calling it, so it stayed broken for the rest of the session. THE CHAIN NOW WORKS END TO END, AND I PROVED IT BY RUNNING IT: a scratch copy with a fake issue titled 'A one-off bell that ends a meeting' queued the spec, derived lan-kit and P2, and wrote the idea into the master list as row 2 with origin 'intake'. LESSON 1 GOES TO x10 - the purest instance yet, a fix-shaped action on the right function with the call never made.

update-kit-and-prs (owner: fix the update kit task failing on the dashboard, and merge any open PR). (1) THE OPEN PRS: exactly ONE in the whole estate - bmi #7, 'Retrofit: let export-kit build the CSV'. I DID NOT MERGE IT, because it CANNOT BE MERGED: mergeable=False, mergeable_state=dirty. Main moved under it (the licence conversion, the mobile fixes, the smoke test all landed after it), so it conflicts. Merging blind would have been worse than leaving it - and its premise is now OBSOLETE anyway: the parity work established that the app's own CSV guard was the better code and folded it INTO export-kit, which is the HARVEST direction. The honest next move is to close it, not merge it. It is also the dashboard's ONLY attention item, so that card is about this PR, not about a failure. (2) THE 'UPDATE KIT' TASK: there is NO workflow by that name in forge. The dashboard's controls are: Refresh project hub, Update profile README, Refresh dashboard data, Metrics, Refresh blog, Refresh store, Refresh plan, Refresh registry, All kit tests, validate skills, Heartbeat. The likely candidates are 'All kit tests' - WHICH I FIXED EARLIER TODAY, it had never run because gh rejects --slurp with --jq - or 'Update profile README'. I could not identify it with certainty from the data, and guessing at which one to change would be worse than asking. (3) A REAL BUG FOUND WHILE LOOKING: the dashboard's data carried 'leaderboard failed: TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes'. FIXED and PROVED: fromisoformat on a bare timestamp returns naive, then compared against an aware NOW; guarded at BOTH parse sites because this leaderboard has already crashed once for a different reason.

kit-tests-two-bugs (owner sent the run URL 40181375393). THAT RUN CONFIRMS THE FAILING TASK IS 'All kit tests', AND THERE WERE TWO BUGS, ONE HIDING THE OTHER. (1) DISCOVERY: gh rejects --slurp with --jq, so the matrix was never built and NO KIT TEST EVER RAN. Fixed earlier today; the dispatched run proves it - discover succeeded and 19 kits actually executed. (2) THE REAL FAILURE THAT WAS HIDDEN: 18 kits passed and ui-kit failed with 'Cannot find module jsdom', because the job runs `node test-node.js` and NEVER RUNS `npm install`. A kit with a dependency could never pass; the other 18 need nothing, which is why it went unseen. Fixed with an install step that warns rather than hard-fails if the install itself breaks. THE DASHBOARD SAID THE SAME THING BOTH TIMES - 'All kit tests - failure' was true for the wrong reason and then for a right one, and the label could not tell you which. LESSON 11: one failure can hide another; a red job is a claim, not a diagnosis.

handoff (owner: what to do now, and how do I get the same work to a new session). THE ANSWER TO THE SECOND QUESTION IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: a new session starts with NO memory, and everything learned here lives in the repos but scattered across LEARNINGS.md, BACKLOG.md, QUEUE/, RUNS.jsonl and registry/ - so it had no way to know where to begin. HANDOFF.md is now that single entry point, and the README points at it. It carries: what the estate is and that forge is the brain; the state as MEASURED not claimed (47 apps, 43 of 43 real apps with the four features, 0 invalid workflows, the kit tests fixed, the idea-box chain proved); the FOUR RULES and why each exists (the parity gate, the demo is the app, one licence everywhere, a spec before a scaffold); the FIVE TRAPS that cost real time (the read-back lies ten times; apps are multi-file so enumerate rather than define; defined is not called; a comment saying FIXED is not evidence; one failure hides another); the next work in order; and how to work here. TO CONTINUE IN A NEW SESSION: say 'read forge/HANDOFF.md and forge/LEARNINGS.md, then continue' - that is the whole onboarding.
